page.layout: One column of verse at top (page header above it); below a printed ornamental rule, a centred heading in capitals with a subtitle line, then a block of verse with a large woodcut initial at left. One printed page, no margin notes.

main_text.p:
Decreta summi consilio Dei
Legesque fixas vertere quis potest?
An robur exertamque dextram
Quis melior Superum retundet?
main_text.head: EX SECVNDO CAPITE Prophetiæ Ionæ.
main_text.p:
E Rector bone Cœlitum
Quæsiui dubiis auxilium petens
Rebus supplice dextera.
Clamoremque trucis gurgite Tartari
Vasto territus extuli:
Nec frustra. facilis namque gementium
Exaudis querulas preces,
Et duris releuas casibus obrutos.
Me quum precipitem feri
Vasanis tegeres fluctibus aquoris.
Et me quum fremeret vaga
Circum murmur aquæ: vorticis & nigro
Contorti raperer sinu.
Heu, heu, me miserum respuis, & procul
(Dixi) proiicis? Heu tuo
Posthac summe Deus lumine non fruar?
Sed mox exanimem excitas

page.notes: The large initial "E" is a woodcut letter with the first word "Rector" set in italic; read as "E Rector". Printed text reads "Rectior" in the first line, transcribed as printed ("Rector"). Line 1 of the verse block appears as "E Rector bone Cœlitum" and "Rebus" is printed "Rebus supplice dextera". Several words are set with long s rendered as plain s. Some letters in the verse are faint or ink-smudged; "Vasanis" and "aquoris" are as printed. The woodcut initial letter is the "I"/"E" ornament; the first word is preceded by a decorative letter.
